newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS FIRE HEAD COACH STEVE KASPER AFTER DISMAL SEASON.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS FIRE HEAD COACH STEVE KASPER AFTER DISMAL SEASON.

text.p: After finishing dead last in the National Hockey League and missing the playoffs for the first time in 30 years, the Boston Bruins fired head coach Steve Kasper on Friday.
Assistant coach Cap Raeder was also relieved of his duties following the dismal 1996-97 campaign.
"This season, obviously, was a disappointment to everyone in the organisation and our fans," assistant general manager Mike O'Connell said in announcing the coaching change.

The Bruins' streak of 29 consecutive playoff appearances -- the longest in the NHL -- came to a halt this year with Boston posting a league-worst 26-47-9 record for 61 points in Kasper's second year behind the bench.
"We know that changes have to be made to improve our team for next year and we felt that this was a change that had to be made," O'Connell said of the decision to fire Kaspar.

"Steve has strengths as a coach but, rightly or wrongly, coaches are judged by their record and the fact is that our record was poor last season. He did an all right job, but the coach's mandate is to win."

Kasper, 35, guided the Bruins to a 40-31-1 record in 1995-96, his first year as coach. Boston lost in the first round of the playoffs last season and the team's fortunes went steadily downhill from there.

"Would it accomplish anything to say, 'We should've done this, we should've done that?' Fact of the matter is I'm not the coach anymore and I can't do anything about it," said Kasper, who spend more than eight years of his 13-season NHL playing career with the Bruins.
Suggesting Bruins' management was as much to blame for the club's demise as his coaching, Kasper said: "I think collectively, we probably all could've done a better job."
